newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal's cotton area up 50 percent in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Senegal's cotton area up 50 percent in 1996/97.

text.p: Senegal's farmers have planted 52,290 hectares of cotton for the 1996/97 season, 50 percent more than the year before, according to data from the state cotton marketing company SODEFITEX.
This should lead to higher output than in recent years, a company official told Reuters.
Senegal's cotton crop, which is harvested between November and February, fell steadily to 28,664 tonnes in 1993/94 from a 50,000 tonnes peak in 1991/92.
The government tried to halt the slide in 1995/96 by raising the produce price to 170 CFA a kg from 150 CFA and paying a 16 CFA a kg bonus. Production rose slightly to 31,350 tonnes.
Officials say the bonus will be raised to 20 CFA a kg next year and they put target production at 50,000 tonnes. The government aims for national output of 100,000 tonnes by 2000.

SODEFITEX has been listed for privatisation. The state currently owns 77.5 percent of the firm, the French development agency Caisse Francaise de Developpement has a 20 percent stake and Compagnie Bancaire de L'Afrique de l'Ouest has 2.5 percent.
